ANSWER OF THE ELECTRIC POWER SUPPLY ASSOCIATION 
 IN SUPPORT OF ISO-NE REQUEST FOR EXTENDED COMMENT PERIOD  
 
 
Pursuant to the November 13, 2026 filing1 from ISO New England, Inc. (“ISO-NE” 
or “the ISO”), the New England Power Pool Participants Committee, the Participating 
Transmission Owners Administrative Committee, on behalf of the Participating 
Transmission Owners (“PTOs”) and a number of PTOs2 in the above-captioned docket, 
the Electric Power Supply Association (“EPSA”)3 respectfully submits this answer in 
support of the ISO-NE’s request for a short extension of the comment period on the 
ISO’s proposed Tariff revisions related to the integration of large loads to its 
 
1  
ISO New England, Inc. et al., Revisions Related to the Integration of Large Loads to the 
Transmission System, Docket No. ER27-484-000 (November 13, 2026). 
2  
These PTOs include: Central Maine Power Company; Connecticut Transmission Municipal 
Electric Energy Cooperative; Eversource Energy Service Company on behalf of The Connecticut Light 
and Power Company, Public Service Company of New Hampshire and NSTAR Electric Company; 
Fitchburg Gas and Electric Light Company; Green Mountain Power Corporation; The Narragansett 
Electric Company d/b/a Rhode Island Energy; New England Power Company d/b/a National Grid; New 
Hampshire Transmission, LLC; The United Illuminating Company; Unitil Energy Systems, Inc.; Vermont 
Electric Cooperative, Inc.; Vermont Transco LLC; and Versant Power. 
3  
EPSA is the national trade association representing competitive power suppliers in the U.S. 
EPSA members provide reliable and competitively priced electricity from environmentally responsible 
facilities using a diverse mix of fuels and technologies. EPSA seeks to bring the benefits of competition to 
all power customers. This pleading represents the position of EPSA as an organization but not 
necessarily the views of any particular member with respect to any issue. EPSA filed a doc-less motion to 
intervene in this proceeding on November 13, 2026.

2 
transmission system. EPSA respectfully requests that the Commission extend the 
deadline for submitting comments to December 7, 2026, as requested by ISO-NE. 
I. ANSWER 
As noted by the ISO, given the breadth of this filing with Tariff Revisions, as well 
as the upcoming holiday, an extension of the comment period in the instant docket to 24 
days, or until December 7, 2026, would help to ensure that interested parties have 
ample time to review and develop comments on the filing, particularly multiple member 
organizations like trade associations and NGOs (“Non-Governmental Organizations”).4 
EPSA therefore agrees with ISO-NE and respectfully requests that the Commission 
grant this request. The short extension would have the added benefit of aligning the 
comment period with the other expected large loads filings that will be filed with the 
Commission on November 16, which would allow stakeholders to take a holistic look at 
these critical proceedings, benefiting the respective records in these multiple 
proceedings.  
II. CONCLUSION 
WHEREFORE, EPSA respectfully requests that the Commission grant ISO-NE’s 
request to extend the comment period in this proceeding, so that comments would be 
due on December 7, 2026.
